questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility to attend a good university, to meet people and explore the city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult after the semester started, alright before then.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any "extra" assistance if any more than the French students. Little information was given by professors or other staff on how exams were conducted and in general how their education was set up.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite hard, students need to look at least 5-6 months prior in my opinion to find good housing for the value. Almost every housing option I found was very expensive for what was provided, which is of course expected in Paris, but this still makes it quite hard for incoming students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Above all they should be very careful and be mindful about who they are renting from - if I were to rent again in Paris I would definitely rent through an agency or an acquaintance since scammers unfortunately are everywhere in big cities like Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were instructed to show up to the main Sorbonne Campus in the 5th and get out student ID's and other info there on how the semester would go. Another day we came to register for classes which was not the best process. We had to wait in a long queue in the heat for a couple hours and then register by paper for classes, and some were filled up so we were told to quickly pick another instead. All in all, what you might expect from an older university but not very effective and smart process in my opinion.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistance from the inscription professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change a couple of them to different classes so I ended up with two classes I didn't want to have 30 ECTS in total, and they also proved to be much harder than the others.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To research as much as they can from home about various subjects and maybe prepare a plan A, B and C just in case so they are well prepared.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very unorganized and often not a satisfactory level of teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses were varied, some were well-organized and well tought with good professors while others were very confusing with quite honestly a bad quality of teaching. Especially my ancient studies and literature classes were confusing and professors were often berating students for innocuous things and etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was generally much better at UCPH, but I think this is because many of my values and what I'm used to is in line with danish education and therefore not the French. In France I experienced a sort of implicite hierarchy in their society and education where I didn't always feel the young students were respected. For example I experienced professors and staff speak and behave rudely to students many times. At UCPH everyone is treated like equal adults and there is no disrespect.

Further, the style of teaching was mostly composed of the teacher explaining concepts by the blackboard for however long the class lasted and there was much less student interaction.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I'm not sure of all their equivalent titles in English so I will list them in French:

1. Grammaire et histoire de la langue
2. Ecrire et penser la fiction
3. Linguistique, sémiotique, communication
4. Sociolinguistique et psycholinguistique
5. Histoire du cinéma
6. Histoire de la culture occidentale pour Lettres Modernes

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
That depends on their chosen bachelor and what courses they've already taken but above all I would say to choose classes you are very interested in and relative to your proficiency level in the given language you are taking them in. It would be best to find a comprise between the two, so you don't end up struggling with a class that's simply too hard either because of the subject matter or the level of language difficulty it's being taught in.
I would therefore recommend a good balance of relevant classes for your bachelor but also some that are just for interest reasons and to balance out your course load.

questions.answer: Transportation, housing, extra things for apartment etc

questions.answer: transportation - a navigo card for students was more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many options such as riding, swimming, running, cinemaclub etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The parismus events and maybe joining their trips around France if there's time because several of my friends said it was a lot of fun and they met a lot of people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore as many of the arrondissements as possible, for example a weekend trip to somewhere outside Paris, trip to Disney, concerts etc

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as I have vacationed many times before in France and there are many similarities in general

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just approach them and ask if they want to hangout at a cafe or go to a concert - I met some very nice French girls because I was going to a concert alone but ended up going with them and got to know them after. Just go for it! All the local students/people I met were all very nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The hierarchal layers of society for one, as I'm not used to addressing people formally in Denmark.
Adjusting to living in a much bigger city - account for more time to arrive to school in the mornings as sometimes it was almost impossible to get on the metro due to overcrowding.
Sometimes processes were quite slow and ineffective compared to Scandinavia in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Almost everywhere I went in the city everyone was seemingly happy and very easy to talk to, there are endless opportunities of things to do in the city, amazing architecture, they value their culture life very highly - often going to museums, concerts and parks and conserving this.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have multiple suggestions for what courses you'd like to take as they are not always all available
2. Find good housing ahead of time to avoid stress
3. Create a good and realistic budget

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Manage expectations: are you going on exchange for academic reasons or to meet new people and try living in another country? Often the latter will be the more giving reason I found. 

For social purposes: to try and "announce" you'll go to Paris through social media if you'd like to meet new people and don't be afraid to grab a coffee and explore the city with them. Often people would post on Facebook, TikTok or Instagram just asking if they wanted to meet up. 

Lastly: remember to experience as much as you can and enjoy it! Especially if you're only on exchange for 1 semester, it passes by very fast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people definitely. They are now some of my best friends and we shared some of my favorite memories together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing and trying to keep up with all the classes and exams, as we had "exams" the DST's almost once every 2 weeks and many more in December - so a very different format than at UCPH.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
